card.name: Linking words in adverse-event warnings
card.fires_on: Small linking words (with, of, occur, who) right after a reported adverse event, such as 'has been reported with' or 'events can occur'. Most often in C. difficile diarrhea warnings about antibacterial agents.

modes.label: C. difficile warning
modes.description: The word 'with' or 'of' after 'has been reported' in the CDAD warning about antibacterial use.
modes.example: Clostridium difficile associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported<< with>> use of nearly all antibacterial agents,

modes.label: Other adverse event statements
modes.description: A linking or verb word after a serious event is named, before timing or the affected group.
modes.example: These events can<< occur>> at any time during use and without warning

card.writes: It seems to push toward words that describe harm or a broad scope, such as 'damage' or 'harm' being suppressed, so the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It fires on the short connecting word in warning sentences like 'has been reported with use of antibiotics'.
